summary: Oregon's sitting senator, Jeff Merkley (Democrat), ran again and won a fourth term, defeating David Brock Smith (Republican) and two other candidates.

candidates.name: Jeff Merkley
candidates.bio: Jeff Merkley was first elected to the U.S. Senate from Oregon in 2008 and previously served as Speaker in the Oregon legislature. He was executive director of a Habitat for Humanity affiliate in Portland before entering politics and sits on the Senate Appropriations and Foreign Relations committees.

positions.summary: Supports raising the minimum wage to a living wage and ending lower minimum wages for tipped, youth and disabled workers.
Supports Medicare for All and has written a bill to let people who buy private insurance enroll in Medicare instead.
Says he supports making sure asylum laws are followed and passing comprehensive immigration reform.
Says he supports lowering the cost of college and backing career and technical education and union apprenticeships.
Says he supports building renewable energy with union labor and stopping new fossil fuel projects.
Says he is working to restore Roe v. Wade protections and end the Hyde Amendment.

candidates.name: David Brock Smith
candidates.bio: David Brock Smith is an Oregon state senator representing the 1st district since 2023. He won the Republican nomination for U.S. Senate in the May 2026 primary.

positions.summary: Says he opposes new taxes and supports incentives for job growth, more affordable homes, and cutting fraud and unnecessary spending.

Spoke against a 2026 Oregon bill that limits masks and requires identification for law enforcement, including federal immigration officers. He said he would never support "the negative perception of public safety."
Was a chief sponsor of House Bill 3375 in 2021, which set a goal of planning for offshore wind energy development.
Voted no in 2017 on House Bill 3391, which requires health plans to cover reproductive health services.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35). Shares refreshed Nov. 25 from the Oregon Secretary of State count (updated Nov. 25, marked unofficial, 2,000,521 ballots). Write-ins are in the total.
